name: What should be included in a home extension bid in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a home extension bid in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a home extension bid in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful home extension bid should be detailed enough to compare contractors on the same scope. It should list demolition, foundation work, framing, roofing, windows, insulation, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, painting, permits, and final cleanup. It should also identify allowances for finish items, since vague allowances can hide major price differences later. Engineering, architectural drawings, and plan-check support should be clearly stated if they are part of the contract. Homeowners should watch for exclusions like utility upgrades, permit fees, appliance costs, landscaping repairs, and temporary protection of the occupied house. If one bid is much lower than the others, it may be missing critical work rather than offering a better price. A strong bid protects both sides by defining scope, schedule, and expectations before construction starts.
